narration: The King's Dance: The Story of Bakisimba
This is Bakisimba. Ancient to present.
on_screen: Title card: Bakisimba · Uganda · Ancient to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated centuries ago in the Buganda Royal Court, attributed to the movements of a drunken King Ssuuna.
It was initially performed to honor ancestors and spirits before evolving into a broader communal practice for unity and pride.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed at weddings, coronations, harvest seasons, and national events.
It serves as a means of storytelling, expressing emotions, and reinforcing community bonds.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers form a circle, with individuals moving to the center to perform.
The style involves vigorous hip movements, stomps, jumps, and specific hand gestures, supported by a group that claps and sings.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: dancers typically form a circle
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is driven by a percussion ensemble including Nseege (gourd rattles), engoombe (cow horn trumpets), and drums such as the Mpuunyi, Nankasa, Mbuut, and Ngalabi.
Listen for the Nseege (gourd rattles), engoombe (cow horn trumpets), Mpuunyi (drum), Nankasa (drum).
A percussion-heavy ensemble featuring the distinct resonance of Ngalabi and other drums, punctuated by the shaking of gourd rattles and the call of cow horn trumpets.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.vocal_style: Singing by the group accompanying the dancers.
music_brief.sound_description: A percussion-heavy ensemble featuring the distinct resonance of Ngalabi and other drums, punctuated by the shaking of gourd rattles and the call of cow horn trumpets.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Bakisimba (Uganda). Instruments: Nseege (gourd rattles), engoombe (cow horn trumpets), Mpuunyi (drum), Nankasa (drum), Mbuut (drum), Ngalabi (drum). Vocal style: Singing by the group accompanying the dancers.. Mood: energetic, rhythmic, celebratory. It should sound like this: A percussion-heavy ensemble featuring the distinct resonance of Ngalabi and other drums, punctuated by the shaking of gourd rattles and the call of cow horn trumpets. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress with a respectful nod (palette and fabric only): the sources describe sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire, or the dance is sacred
care: every element traceable to the costume notes or a licensed image; nothing added for effect
no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
credits name the tradition and the sources of the reconstruction
